FINDING (high, correctness): F002 still accepts a forged held-lock token, so direct write mode is not actually restricted to a real F005-held sidecar lock. Evidence: [invocation_ledger.py](/Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic-canonical-discovery/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/invocation_ledger.py:391) exposes `_LOCK_GUARD`, and `HeldLedgerLock(target=..., _guard=il._LOCK_GUARD).authorizes(...)` returns `True` without acquiring `hold_ledger_lock()`; [canonical_backfill.py](/Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic-canonical-discovery/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/canonical_backfill.py:333) trusts only `isinstance` plus `authorizes`. Recommendation: make write authorization prove an actually-held OS lock, or keep construction fully inside a closure/private class path that callers cannot forge; add a regression test using `il._LOCK_GUARD`.
